title: Jaipur rug brand cut a 41-day decor purchase cycle to 26 days with a WhatsApp consideration engine
content: SITUATION: A Jaipur D2C home-decor brand (handcrafted rugs, AOV ₹18,400) spent ₹9.2L/month on Meta and Google. Meta looked healthy at 3.1 ROAS on last-click, but the real leak was hidden: median time-to-purchase was 41 days first-click-to-order, 72% of add-to-carts never converted, and retargeting frequency had crept to 7.3 at ₹480 CPM. Buyers loved a ₹18,400 rug, then went silent for weeks comparing with Pepperfry and local artisans — true CAC was ₹5,900, not the ₹3,000 last-click implied. ACTION: We stopped treating this as a top-funnel reach problem. Every PDP and abandoned cart pushed a WhatsApp opt-in for a free 'room styling' consult. A human-plus-template flow sent fabric swatches, a 90-second YouTube room-fit video, and EMI options (₹1,533/month) on day 2, 9 and 21 — and captured room dimensions for accurate follow-ups. We shifted ₹2L out of cold prospecting into this nurture layer. OUTCOME: Over 90 days WhatsApp opt-in hit 34% of carts, the consideration window fell from 41 to 26 days, blended ROAS rose from 3.1 to 4.6, and CAC dropped from ₹5,900 to ₹4,100.
lesson: For high-AOV, long-consideration D2C, the bottleneck is rarely top-funnel reach — it's the silent weeks between interest and purchase, where last-click ROAS lies and retargeting frequency just burns money. Own that gap with a permission-based WhatsApp nurture that removes the specific buying frictions (fit, EMI, trust) instead of re-showing the same ad. The consult is also your data moat: capture room dimensions and budget once, and every follow-up converts harder.
